newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania C.Bank seen intervening on forex market.
newsitem.headline: Romania C.Bank seen intervening on forex market.

text.p: Operators on Romania's foreign exchange market said on Wednesday that the central bank had intervened to prop up the leu currency, which rose to 7,000/00 to the dollar from an opening of 8,200/00 to 8,900/00.
"The National (central) Bank has intervened and sold dollars today," one dealer with the private Ion Tiriac Bank told Reuters.
The central bank (BNR) declined to confirm intervening on the market.

A BNR spokesman said the bank -- which has so far refrained from stepping in to support the sagging leu which has fallen from 4,100 since January 1 -- would make an announcement at a press conference on Friday.
"The BNR has sold dollars in a bid to soak up leu liquidities from the market," a dealer said.

Traders said slackening demand for dollars had also been influenced by Tuesday's announcement that Romanian electricity authority Renel was raising $150 million from international markets, in a corporate bond issue led by Merrill Lynch.
A dealer said the BNR's intervention had not been a massive one, but that the central bank wanted to "send a signal to the market," following a recent drive to tighten its monetary policies.
Operators expected the central bank to further reduce the amount on offer at its auction for refinancing credits on Thursday, which they said would further whet "leu hunger."
Latest official data put the BNR's own reserves at $812.2 million in January.
